`“――――Whew”
`One long breath finally calms me.
`“Why am I running away?”
`Once I calm down, my senses return.
`I have not done anything wrong, so there was no need to flee the house.\

`“―――Unbelievable. I look like a complete idiot.”
`Going back to the mansion now and meekly eating breakfast would look even more ridiculous.
`“―――Might as well go to school.”
`With a sigh, I start down the hill toward the residential district.\

; 学校校門（朝）<左カーテン(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_01a.jpg",%type_lcartain_mid

`―――I arrive a full half hour earlier than usual.
`Only a scattering of students stand near the front gate; apparently I am the only one who comes to school at such an awkward hour\

; 学校外観（朝）<左カーテン(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_03a.jpg",%type_lcartain_mid


`The sports clubs are holding morning practice on the field.
`I am not in a club now, but I do enjoy moving my body.
`My athletic ability is good enough that I can take a little pride in it.
br
`But I cannot join a club.
`Chronic anemia means I may let everyone down when they need me most―――and my doctor has strictly forbidden me from exercising too often.\

`Ever since middle school, I have been invited to join clubs more times than I can count.
`Each time I turn them down with the same line, “It is not really me.”
`And each refusal leaves me feeling―――some nameless distance between us.
`In the end.
`Perhaps it has always been an unconscious wall: the knowledge that, no matter what I do, I can never join the people on the other side.\

`“……………”
`Enough. This is not like me. I cut the pointless sentimentality short and head for the classroom.\

; 黒画面<左カーテン(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_lcartain_mid
; 教室（朝）<左カーテン(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_06a.jpg",%type_lcartain_mid
;CD-DA「学校・昼」
play "*3"

`“Huh―――”
`I expect to be first, but several classmates are already here.\

`“Hey, Tohno; you are early.”
`“Morning. I never knew this class had so many people with nothing better to do.”
`“Like hell. We just finished morning practice. Normally, the only person who comes this early without belonging to a club is whoever is on classroom duty.”
br
`Put that way, he has a point.
`I exchange greetings with the others and sit down.
`Homeroom is still half an hour away.
`Watching the classroom gradually fill might not be such a bad way to pass the time.\

; 黒画面<クロスフェード(中)>
bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_lshutter_mid
; 教室（朝）<左シャッター(中)>
bg "image\bg\bg_06a.jpg",%type_lshutter_mid


`At seven-fifty, the classroom begins to fill with chatter.
`“―――Huh?”
`I think I catch a glimpse of her in the hall.\

`“Back in the first-year corridor again―――what is she doing?”
`Maybe she came to see me.
`If so―――
br



return

`I swallow.
`Arcueid’s gaze fixes squarely on me.
`It is as though―――if I move even slightly, she will attack at once.\

`“This―――this makes no sense, Arcueid.
`Nrvnqsr is supposed to be dead. So why are vampire killings still happening? Do not tell me you are―――”\
; 中央<夜>=アルクェイド:楽04（腕組、ちょっと不機嫌そう）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t03.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Of course not. It was another member of a vampiric species.”
`The tension leaves her at once, and Arcueid answers with open exasperation.
`I am not convinced.\

`“What does that mean? Are you saying vampires will keep appearing one after another?”
; 中央<夜>=アルクェイド:楽04（腕組、ちょっと不機嫌そう）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Don’t be ridiculous. Those serial murders have been the work of a single member of a vampiric species from the beginning. No new member has arrived, and Nrvnqsr had nothing to do with the case at all.”
br
`――――What?
`Even Nrvnqsr had nothing to do with them?
br
`“Wh―――what do you mean?”
`“Exactly what I said. Honestly, Shiki, you are sharp in some ways and astonishingly dense in others. Listen. Nrvnqsr may have belonged to a vampiric species, but did you ever see him drink anyone’s blood?”\
; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst


`“Drink blood, when he ate people whole, crunching them up from the head―――oh”
br
`I see.
`How did I miss something so simple?
`The victims of these killings have all been found drained of blood.\

`Nrvnqsr was different.
`He left no corpses. He did not merely drink blood—he devoured even flesh, erasing every trace.
`The people he ate at the hotel were treated as missing persons, not murder victims.
br
`Then―――his acts were plainly different from the killings taking place around the city.\

`“Wait. Then what are these murders? Who the hell has been doing them?”
; 中央<夜>=アルクェイド:楽04（腕組、ちょっと不機嫌そう）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t03.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Like I said, another member of a vampiric species, one other than Nrvnqsr, is responsible; to be exact, I came to this city because that creature was here, and Nrvnqsr came because he was chasing me. That is the chain of events.”
`“―――What? Then the enemy you were hunting was not Nrvnqsr?!”\

; 中央<夜>=アルクェイド:楽04（腕組、ちょっと不機嫌そう）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Right. I never said Nrvnqsr was my target, did I?
`I was his target, but he was never mine; my only target was the vampire this city calls its serial murderer.”
; 中央<夜>=アルクェイド:楽04（腕組、ちょっと不機嫌そう）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t11.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“…Shiki, don’t tell me you made some incredibly basic mistake.”\
; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst


`“Wh―――――”
`I suck in a stunned breath.
`But―――Arcueid is right.
`When she said she was here to kill a vampire, I jumped to the conclusion that she meant Nrvnqsr――――
br
`“…Then are you saying that fighting Nrvnqsr that night was completely pointless?!”\

; 中央<夜>=アルクェイド:楽04（腕組、ちょっと不機嫌そう）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“It wasn’t pointless. You fought him in my place, didn’t you? Though none of it would have happened if you hadn’t killed me first.”
br
`“――――――”
`The world tilts around me.\

`“So Nrvnqsr had nothing to do with the vampire murders, and another vampire has been terrorizing the city this entire month?”
`“Yes, exactly. But that is my problem to handle, so you need not worry about it. More importantly, Shiki”\
;CD-DA停止
playstop

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst

`With a strangely delighted smile, Arcueid looks up at me as I stand there dumbfounded.
br
`“How was last night? Who showed up?”\




return

`“This power is magnificent, isn’t it, Shiki?

`I could ask for no more formidable partner.”\

`“You want me to join you?”
; 中央<夜>=ロア（ダークシキ）:通常<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\roa_t04c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“No. I’m not asking you to join me. I am going to make you mine. Your wishes are irrelevant. If anything, they would only get in the way.
`Rest easy―――once I have drained your blood and stolen your soul. I will elevate you into a being capable of wielding your power without the slightest hesitation.”\

`“I see. Then one more question.
`What do you see, lines or points? No—let me make it simpler. You only see them on living creatures, don’t you? You can’t see them on anything else.”
`“What? Of course: things without life have no life to begin with. The place life comes from can exist only in a living thing.”
`“――――I thought so. Now it all makes sense, vampire.”
br
`I tightened my grip on the knife.
`Pain had conquered my mind; there was only one thing left in my sight.\

; 中央<夜>=ロア（ダークシキ）:通常<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\roa_t04a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Strange—those are hardly suitable last words, but no matter; our conversation is over. I still have that Church woman to find and dispose of.
`―――Rejoice, Shiki. Once I have made you my thrall, she will be your first victim.”

; 中央を消去<左シャッター(中)>
cl c,%type_lshutter_mid

br
`Roa was coming.
`My distorted vision could no longer make out his shape.\

`“――You and I don’t see the same thing, SHIKI.”
br
`Deep inside my head.
`A switch clicked on.\

`“All you see is life. You understand nothing about death. That’s why you couldn’t kill me, and why you could only kill a woman already at death’s door.”
br
`My brain burned white-hot.
br
`“―――What…?”\

`“If you truly saw death, you couldn’t stay sane. All you recognize are the places that keep things alive.
`If you saw death―――there’s no way you could remain standing.”\

`“To see the ‘death’ of things is to be plunged into the realization that everything in this world is uncertain and fragile.
`The ground may as well not exist; the sky looks ready to fall at any moment.”
`“What are you―――what are you talking about?”\
`Roa’s voice had begun to shake.
`Of course it had.
`He could not understand even a fraction of what I was saying.
br

`―――That is what it means to see death.
`These eyes aren’t some wonderful power I could ever boast of, the way you do.”\

br

`“Van-ish, vanishing, I am vanishing――――”

`The curtains swayed back and forth.
`Outside, the sky was beautifully clear,
`and a dry wind announced the end of summer.\

`“Pleased to meet you, Shiki Tohno. Congratulations on your recovery.”

`“Shiki, do you understand what I’m saying?”
`“No… Why am I in a hospital?” “You don’t remember.
`You were involved in a car accident while you were walking down the street.
`A shard of glass went into your chest. It wasn’t the sort of wound anyone should have survived.”
`Still smiling, the man in white said something that didn’t sound like a doctor at all.\
br
br
br
br
br
br
`――――――I felt horribly,
`horribly sick.\

`“I’m sleepy. Can I go to sleep?” “Of course.
`Don’t strain yourself. For now, you should concentrate on getting well.”
`The doctor kept smiling.
`I could hardly stand to look at him.
`“Doctor, can I ask you something?”
`“What is it, Shiki?”
`“Why do you have scribbles all over your body? This room is full of cracks too. It looks like it might fall apart any second.”
br
`For the briefest instant, the doctor’s smile slipped. Then it returned, as cheerful as ever, and he strode away with his heels clicking.\

`“There does seem to be something wrong with his brain. Call Dr. Ashiya in neurosurgery. His eyes may be damaged as well; schedule an examination for this afternoon.”
br
`The doctor whispered this to a nurse so that I wouldn’t hear.\

`They had to be seams: weak places,
`like the skin where an operation had been stitched closed.
`Otherwise, there was no way a child like me could cut through a wall.
br

`You have only two choices: fight or be killed. If you cannot fight, then all that remains is death.”
`Click by measured click.
`She approached.\

`“―――――――!”
`My body sprang.
`My back, shoulder, and arm were nearly dead, yet it leapt as if such injuries were trivial.
br
`―――I could scarcely believe it myself.
`Breathing raggedly, I raced into the school building at a speed nearly equal to hers.\

;S.E.停止
wavestop

; 黒画面<左カーテン(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_lcartain_fst
!w1000

play "*8"

; 学校廊下2（夜）<左カーテン(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_11c.jpg",%type_lcartain_fst

`“Hah, hah, hah, hah―――――” I ran.
`Without thought,
`wanting only to escape from something, I kept running.\

`“Hah, hah, hah, hah―――――”
`At last I reached my limit.
`Maybe I had run out of breath; maybe my wounds had finally robbed my limbs of movement.
`There was little difference between them now.\

`“Hah, hah, hah――――――”
`I reached the end of the corridor.
`I struck the wall where the path ended and collapsed.
`Flat on my back, I tried to force strength into my limbs, then realized how absurd that was.\

`“Hah—hah—hah.”
`I sat slumped on the floor with my legs loosely crossed and rested my back against the wall.
`I drew up my knees, tipped my face back, and took a deep breath.\

`“―――――The moon.”
`Moonlight shone through the window above me.
`Perhaps it was exhaustion.
`Everything I could see looked hollow, blurred beneath a veil of mist.
br
`Hollow.
`Did that mean uncertain?
`As uncertain as I was. As uncertain as the human being called Shiki Tohno.\

`“…Hur… ts…”
`My shoulder throbbed.
`If only I had been as solid and certain as this pain, would any of this have happened?\

`I no longer understood.
`I had lived my entire life believing I was Shiki Tohno.
`But apparently there was another Shiki, and I was an adopted child of unknown origin.
`An adopted child should have memories from before entering the Tohno household, yet I had none.
`I truly possessed no memories except those of Shiki Tohno.\

; 黒画面<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
; 月（画面いっぱい）<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_01.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`A solitary moon hangs in the night sky.
`“――――”
`How strange.
`How did I never notice before?
`Tonight is so―――\

; 学校廊下2（夜）<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_11c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

br
`…In the end, what had I ever been?
`I knew nothing about myself, and now even that self was about to disappear. It was ridiculous.
br
`Everything was indistinct and absurd.
`A world where death could be seen.
`Eyes that saw death.
`That day eight years ago.
`I met the woman who taught me how to live, and because of her I had managed a normal life.
`Even now, I could say without doubt that meeting her had been right.\

`“…But, Teacher, it seems I was someone who never should have been allowed to live.”
`Perhaps I ought to end my life while enough of me remained to believe that.
`But I couldn’t.
`I could not kill myself.
`However wretched or mistaken my life might be, I had lived it.\

`If I died, everything would become a lie.
`I wanted to live.
`No matter how wrong I was, no matter how much I might lose, I wanted to live.
br
`If only I still had her.
`If only Ciel had remained beside me, I would not have cared what else I lost.\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――For that alone, I kept myself alive. But now even that is over.
`Five years. I cannot really say whether they were long or short.\

`“…Liar.”
`I never wanted to hear those words.\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――I am grateful to you, Tohno.
`My work is finished now. All that remains is to fulfill the responsibility I still bear.\

`“…You liar.”
`Yet perhaps there had been truth as well. She deceived me, yes—but not even once had she ever—\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――Thank you for everything. I cannot remember the last time I was this happy.
`So let us shake hands one final time.\

`“—Oh, you liar.”
`Not once. Not once had she actually lied to me.\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――After I am gone, please stay friends with Inui.
`I wanted to be a student like you and him――――\

`“…”
`But her very existence had been the lie.
`Even so, I cannot believe that smile was false.\

`But this is what reality amounts to.
`Ciel was a lie.
`She stayed beside me only so that she could kill me.
`I had been deceived.
`She had never loved me.
`Helping me when I was falling apart, wasting our breaks together for no reason—every moment of it was only meant to determine whether I was Roa.\

`My teeth grind.
`I clamp my jaw until my molars ache.
br
`“…Damn it.”
`Bitter with frustration, I claw at the wall.
`Yes. I had been deceived.
`Every step Ciel took toward me was calculated.\

`“…And yet…”
`My fingertips brush the wall, aching with a grief I cannot name.
`Yes, she deceived me.
`But even so――――
br
`“―――I can’t hate her.”
!w1000

\

`I could never hate her.
`Even if it was a lie to her, I was happy.
`Nothing can make that untrue.
`I knew her for less than two weeks, and yet I had been so―――so genuinely happy.
br
`“Damn it――――”
`That is why I cannot hate her.
`Yet that illusion belonged to me alone.
`That alone is what makes it so bitter.\

; 月（画面いっぱい）<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_01.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`My vision blurs.
`Beyond the window lies a white night.
`The silent school seems sunk at the bottom of the sea,
`wavering gently around me.
br
`Everything is false, a vision that vanishes when approached.
`One vast mirage, forever beyond my grasp.

`We watch the passing cars and discuss one meaningless subject after another.
`The most meaningless subject of all is our respective abilities.
`My eyes, which can see the death of things,
`and his body, which is exceedingly difficult to kill.
`As we compare their workings—
`“Wait. Does that mean you could kill the five senses?”
`It makes no sense at all.\

`“No. I can’t kill something so vague it can only be expressed in abstractions.”
`“Bullshit. To kill sight, destroy the eyes; to kill hearing, destroy the ears. Even I could do that.
`But you’re different. You can kill a thing without crushing it. If you can see those lines, then what you’re killing isn’t the object—it’s the meaning.
`So you ought to be able to scrape away things beyond the five senses too――――whatever people call a sixth sense for convenience, souls, emotions, things like that.”\

`“Huh.”
`He may be right.
`My eyes are intrinsically abnormal.
`Trying to explain them with ordinary logic was a mistake from the outset.
br
`Could I kill that, then?
`The mirage I saw once as a child.
`The possessing spirit called something like kurenai sekishu.\

`“But that sounds difficult. If I started seeing things like that, I don’t think I’d be able to think straight.”
`“Naturally. You’d be trying to perform God’s calculations with nothing but a human brain. Anyone normal would end up a vegetable.”
`With that, the man stands and returns to the vending machine.\

`“Hey.”
`Still facing the machine, he holds a hand out behind him.
`I toss another coin, which he catches neatly, and he buys more canned coffee.
`After taking a drink, the man says,
!w750
br
`“Been a long time since I talked to a human being.”
!w750
br
`That is what he says.\

`“That’s an odd remark. Have you been living on a deserted island?”
`“Still am. This deserted island right here. Apparently I’m out of step with society. They say anyone who kills for no reason can’t be sane.
`So when someone out of step like me talks to people who aren’t, we can’t have a real conversation.”\

`“I see. So we’re out of step.”
`“Right. Which side is abnormal doesn’t matter. The side standing outside society is the one that’s out of step.”
`“Is that so? Perhaps society is the abnormal one.”
`“Oh—what do you mean by that?”
`“Exactly what I said. You mentioned it yourself.
`It’s like a majority vote. The minority who disagree with everyone else are discarded as ‘useless.’
`It doesn’t matter which side is right. Anyone who fails to fit with the majority gets shut out, right or wrong. There can be no universal standard for being out of step.”\

`“―――――Hmph. So what—murderers like us aren’t villains?”
`“Who knows. I don’t know anything about good or evil. I only mean that, logically, we aren’t the ones out of step.
`Take boxers, for example. It doesn’t have to be boxing, but that makes the idea easy to explain.”\

`“A boxer’s job is to trade blows. But that isn’t all. They put themselves through the misery of cutting weight and train every day to hit people. How to strike more skillfully. How to bring someone down more efficiently. Day after day they hone that single ability like a knife.
`What do you think of that?”
`“Huh. People like that exist? Go on.”\

`“That’s all.
`They fight, but they aren’t supposed to finish the other person off. Accidents happen, of course, and sometimes somebody dies. Yet when that happens, it generally isn’t treated as murder. Isn’t that incredible?”
br
`“―――You mean they’re allowed to kill?”
br
`“No, no. They aren’t allowed to kill. But they are allowed to kill. Quite a contradiction, isn’t it? And there’s more. Apparently a boxer’s fists can be treated as deadly weapons, so boxers aren’t supposed to get into street fights.”\

`“That’s remarkable. Everyone knows a boxer’s fists are weapons, so why does boxing exist at all? If something can kill people, shouldn’t society abolish it?
`Killing is wrong.
`Yet the world overflows with instruments for killing, and even the law approves of them. Then it turns around and says murder is forbidden. You can only call that chaos. If common sense is truly as decent as most people imagine, then we aren’t out of step at all.
`The world is the thing that has strayed from common sense.”\

`Not that I bear any hostility toward boxing.
`Of all the professions in the world, few demand such complete self-denial in pursuit of a single goal.
`A boxer rejects every temptation and forges his own body.
`Human beings are fascinated by strength they can readily understand. That is why contests will never disappear.
`Among all competitors, those who choose a sport built on hurting others are possessed by something special.\

`A longing for strength.
`A mind capable of caring for nothing else.
`Surely that is an exceedingly healthy spirit.
`It may share the same colors as the way this man and I think—we can find meaning only in results—but its form is altogether different.\

`A calling one can throw oneself into so completely that everything else disappears.
`That is not something a person is free to choose.
`Some worship scholarship, some immolate themselves for art, and some throw themselves into commerce.
`If each person could choose that calling, the world would make a cleaner, more comprehensible puzzle.
`But this puzzle is riddled with holes.
`Pieces are missing everywhere, while others belong to a wholly different design.\

`“Huh. You talk a lot. I had a friend like you once.
`How can I put it? He had nothing, so perhaps that was why he seemed to want nothing.
`There was something fiercely aloof about him. But aloofness is only another word for loneliness, isn’t it? I could never stop thinking about him.”
`“I see. Wanting nothing. What about you? Is there anything you want?”
`“I don’t know. Feels like there was, but I can’t remember. How about you?”\

`“Everyone wants something. I had simply never found anything that could consume me.
`The kind of fever in which you lose yourself―――tonight may have been my first.”
`“Ha! Then when all is said and done, you’re a murderer too.”
`“I don’t know. There still isn’t enough evidence to be certain. What about you? Is killing people enjoyable?”
`“――――Are you stupid? If it were fun, I’d never stop doing it. There’s no reason behind this. Once I begin, I become absorbed. That’s all.”\

`I see.
`That, at least, I can partly understand.
`It is not a matter of enjoying murder, but of whether one can lose oneself completely in the work once the act has begun.
br
`Apparently, that is the distinction between being out of step and being ordinary.\

`“Hey. Were you the sort of child who took radios apart?”
`“Ray Dio…? No, I’ve never cut up a guy by that name.”
`“―――All right, thank you for that awful joke. Mine was a joke too, by the way. Living things and machines are opposites. People like us might actually make fairly good doctors.”
`“A doctor, huh? I hate drugs. When they inject you, you can feel yourself thinning away. It’s as if you’ve been reduced to somebody else’s puppet.”\

`Perhaps that is how it feels.
`I already have my own doctor, so medicine has been an everyday fact of life for me for years.\

`“―――――Ah, well. That really was fun.”
`The man rises.
br
`Then he looks down at me――――with eyes emptied of all emotion.
`“―――Now then. There isn’t room for two of us in one city. Put two lions in a cage this small and neither can even claim a territory.”
`His hand moves toward his knife.
`His killing intent is cold and inorganic.
`He genuinely means to fight me to the death.\

`“You shouldn’t.”
`The words leave me with perfect ease.
`“Why not?”
`“As living creatures go, you’re stronger than I am.”
br
`――――But in a fight to the death.
br
`“I’m better than you.”\

`“――――――, ――――――”
`His teeth grind together.
`A twisted smile forms on his face, and then
`“Ha—aha, ah-hahahahaha!”
`he bursts into thunderous laughter.\

`“What? Was it really that funny, murderer?”
`He keeps giggling in short, nervous bursts.
`Just as I decide to leave him to it, the laughter stops dead and he looks at me.
br
`“――――Yes. You’re right.”
br
`With that, the man turns and walks away alone.\

`“This means my time is up. Now that somebody like you has appeared, I’m the one who has to leave town.”
`“I have no intention of taking your place.”
`“No, no, you won’t have a choice. Tonight was the first time you ever lost yourself in something, wasn’t it? Tomorrow will be the same. You won’t endure even one day without it.
`Well, here’s hoping we never meet again.”
`He raises one hand and departs.\

`“――――――――”
`Hearing that we will never meet again leaves me faintly disappointed.
`Roughly ten empty coffee cans lie at my feet.
`Evidently he will never repay what he owes me.\

`I embrace myself—this waking self, this body with a heart unmistakably beating inside it.

`When I first went to live with the Arimas, Akiha apparently came to see me several times.

`My throat dries.
`The dog’s drawn-out howl pounds against my eardrums.

`The blue sky.

`As far as I knew, it was the first time she had ever ventured outside the mansion.\

`the girl untied the ribbon from her hair and placed it in my hand.
`It must have been a parting gift, but I was only a child and felt no particular joy in it.
br
`After all, I doubt any nine-year-old boy would be delighted to receive a ribbon.\

`“That ribbon is my favorite, so make sure you return it to me later.”
`Those words saved me.
br
`Return it to me, the girl said.
`Return to me, I heard.
br
`――――That alone was enough.
`It was the last day, and not one person came to see me off.
`I was glad she had said it—even though we had never spoken before.\

`―――But I could not tell her, “I’ll be sure to return it.”
br
`Of course, at a time like that, I had to be clever enough to understand that I would never be allowed to return to this house.
br
`That was all we said.
`The girl’s eyes were cold as ice, yet there was something sad in them.
`When the time came, I walked back toward the entrance.
`She remained where she was, standing like a doll and watching me go.\

br
br
br
br
br
br
`blue sky.
`not one cloud—a faraway dream of one bright day.\

ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t03.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst


`“Of course, but why stay standing? Your body still hasn't adjusted, Shiki, so why don't you lie down?”
`“Idiot. You're the one who should lie down. Daylight is hard on you, isn't it? Forget about me and talk from bed.”


; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽01（基本的楽）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst


`“No, that would be a waste. Now that I finally have the chance to talk to you, I want to see your face.”
`With a faint smile, Arcueid looked straight into my eyes.\

`“If that's what you want, I suppose I don't mind.”
`I looked away and sat on the edge of the bed.

; すべて消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl a,%type_crossfade_fst

;CD-DA停止
playstop

`Following my lead, Arcueid settled onto the sofa.\

;CD-DA「伝奇その一」
play "*4"

`“Then tell me this.
`That man yesterday―――the one you called Nrvnqsr, what exactly is he?
`I'm asking seriously, so don't give me some ridiculous answer about a magician who pulls crocodiles out of his body.”\

; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t04.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“I wouldn't say anything so ridiculous.
`As you probably guessed, he is another vampire. Among us he is known as Nrvnqsr—an extreme aberration.
`To tell the truth, he is not someone I can talk about so casually.”
`“……”
`So he really was a vampire.
`Yet somehow―――just as Arcueid before me does not fit my idea of a vampire, neither does he.\

`“What kind of man is this Nrvnqsr? You seemed to know him.”
`“Hardly. I have no vampire acquaintances. The moment I become acquainted with one is generally the moment I kill them. Yesterday was the first time I ever met one face-to-face and then parted company.”\

`“But the two of you talked about all sorts of things.”
`“That hardly makes us acquaintances.
`Nrvnqsr is a reasonably famous vampire, and my own name is well known among their kind, so introductions were unnecessary.
`Naturally, the older a vampire becomes and the stranger his abilities, the farther his name spreads.
`Nrvnqsr is exceptional even among them.
`He is one of the ancient vampires, yet an eccentric wanderer with neither castle nor territory.
`For some reason, the Church gave him the epithet Chaos.”\

`“Chaos? What does that mean?”
`“It means complete disorder. Everything is jumbled together.
`Like the primordial Earth, with all sorts of things churning together and no way to know what might emerge; judging from last night, perhaps that is what they meant.”
`“No way to know what might emerge…?”\

; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t02.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Honestly, Shiki. You saw what was inside him. I think I explained before: the longer a vampire lives, the harder it becomes to repair damage to the body.
`A human life simply isn’t high-grade enough material to restore a vessel that has existed for centuries.
`So they absorb beasts and Demonic Beasts—creatures with superior vitality—and remake them into their own flesh.
`Nrvnqsr is said to be among the oldest vampires, so perhaps the number of beasts he has absorbed as substitutes for his body is simply beyond comparison.”\

`“Beyond comparison―――so even those black dogs were parts of Nrvnqsr’s body?”
; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Yes, but a human vessel has limits. At most, it should be able to control around thirty animals as its own body.
`If it absorbed even one member of the Phantasmal Species—the creatures classed as Demonic Beasts or Phantasmal Beasts—that alone would exceed its capacity.
`So all of Nrvnqsr’s familiars probably belong to species that still exist today.
`In that sense, we may have been lucky.”
br
`I didn't understand the last part, but did that mean there might be as many as thirty black dogs?\

`“No, wait. The black dogs weren’t the only things loose in the hotel. I think I saw lions and leopards too.”
; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t02.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“I thought so. Controlling thirty animals of one species is possible, but governing different beasts together inside his body proves Nrvnqsr’s will truly is extraordinary.
; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t03.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`Still, it is odd that someone with such a powerful will would use nothing but wild animals as his body. He ought to be capable of subjugating an exceptionally powerful Demonic Beast――――”
`Arcueid fell silent, pondering the question.\

; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Well, never mind. At least we know his arsenal consists of twenty or thirty familiars.
`And I think I understand a little better where the name Nrvnqsr came from.”
`“What? Nrvnqsr isn’t his real name?”
`“No, Dead Apostles who have lived a long time generally stop using their human names.
`Since they seldom name themselves, the Church assigns names to them instead.
`Every time a new trait is discovered, another piece gets added, so some of them end up with names as long as spells.”\

`“I imagine the Church first called him Nrvnqsr because they particularly despised him.
`Think about it: in a confined hunting ground like a hotel, one lion would be enough to deal with a mere hundred humans. Yet unleashing every beast in his body just to feed that way is wasteful beyond belief.”
; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst
`“……”
`Thirty beasts inside Nrvnqsr.
`Was that alone enough to devour every one of the hundred people fleeing through the hotel, all in thirty minutes?\


`“――――I can’t believe it. That makes him nothing but a monster.”
; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t05b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Yes. Nrvnqsr is about as terrible an opponent as one could meet. He is exactly the kind I would rather never meet.
`But the worst thing is that he found us.
`Even now, this room is certainly being watched by his familiars.”
`“What――――”
`“Of course it is. The sunrise saved us earlier, but tonight there will be no such escape. He knows where I am, so he’ll come to kill me at the ideal hour: midnight.”\

`“He’s coming to kill you tonight?”
; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t02.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Yes—he said so himself.”
; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst


br
`――――What the hell?
`That man―――the man in the black coat—is coming here tonight?\

`“――――――”
`I do not know what to say.
`I know the sensible choice is to run.
`But Arcueid is in this condition.
`Even if she fled, I cannot imagine her escaping a monster like that.\

`No—forget Arcueid; I have to think about myself.
`If I stay here―――if I remain involved with her, I will meet him again.
br
`That man is dangerous.
`There is nothing sane about him.
`Even setting aside the animals inside his body, his eyes looked like a machine’s.
br
`They held no emotion whatsoever.
`They were the eyes of a true killer, one who performs the task assigned to him as naturally as breathing.
`Having nearly died at his hands once, I know in my bones that he is someone I must never confront again.\

`“―――――”
`But can I run alone and leave Arcueid here?
`Whatever she may be, she can barely move because she protected me; can I tell her good luck and walk away――――
br
`“Arcueid, I――――”\

; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Still, there’s nothing to worry about. Nrvnqsr is no match for you, Shiki. Whatever your opponent may be, you can kill it in a single strike.”
`“―――――――Huh?”
br
`Something outrageous.
`Arcueid says it with the air of stating the obvious.\

;CD-DA停止
playstop

`“W-wait―――what on earth are you talking about?”
; 中央<昼>=アルクェイド:楽03（髪を掻き揚げている）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t01b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“You’re going to fight beside me, aren’t you, Shiki?”
`Arcueid gazes straight at me.
`Her eyes are full of absolute trust.
`But this is no joke.
`I―――――
br



return

; 屋外一般 : 公園・路地裏 : 公園Ｂ（死の線あり）<瞬時表示>

`No—it’s too soon.
`Nrvnqsr has only just arrived.
`I need him to focus―――on Arcueid a little longer, or I will never manage a surprise attack.\

; 左<夜>=アルクェイド:睨み03（02のさらにキツイ感じ）<クロスフェード(速)>

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst
; 左<夜>=アルクェイド:睨み03（02のさらにキツイ感じ）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t07.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Is that so? You both pursued me all the way to this country, which seems rather similar to me.”

`“Enough. By that measure, your own caprice is far more extravagant.
`You exist to execute the surviving Dead Apostles, so why pursue the Serpent of Akasha with such tenacity? The Serpent cannot be venom potent enough to merit the obsession of the Princess of the True Ancestors.”\

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst

`Nrvnqsr’s voice rises ever so slightly.
`Arcueid’s taunts must be working: he has eyes only for the white woman who is his enemy.

`―――What do I do?
